dedupe_keys.name: ionospheric irregularity roti maps from the indonesian gnss network ina cors

description: Researchers of Indonesia's National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) publish maps of the rate of TEC change index (ROTI), a measure of ionospheric irregularities such as equatorial plasma bubbles that cause GNSS scintillation and loss of lock, derived from the more than 300 receivers of the Indonesia Continuously Operating Reference Stations (Ina-CORS) run by the Geospatial Information Agency (BIG). TEC is computed from 30-second RINEX data with Seemala's GPS-TEC software, ROTI is the standard deviation of the TEC rate over 5 minutes, and two-dimensional maps are drawn at the 350 km pierce-point height on a 0.25 degree grid, smoothed over 5 by 5 cells, every 10 minutes from 09:00 to 23:50 UT, with sunset and sunrise terminators. Coverage: Indonesia and nearby Southeast Asia, 95 to 140 degrees east and 5 degrees north to 10 degrees south, 2023 and 2024 on Zenodo, with current maps on BRIN's web portal. Format and access: daily archives of map images, about 4.8 GB, and a web viewer, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: maps, not numeric grids; night-time window only; the underlying RINEX data are not shared. Simulation uses: equatorial space weather exposure of GNSS positioning, aviation and timing services in Southeast Asia. Related records: the CAS global TEC maps and the Svalbard collection cover global and polar conditions.
